stem: How does the author’s language in the quotation from Kokoro DIFFER from the author’s language in the quotation from “The List”?

options.label: A
options.text: The author’s language in the quotation from Kokoro illustrates the character’s eager anticipation of an upcoming deadline, while the language in the quotation from “The List” illustrates the character’s feeling of dread about an upcoming deadline.

options.label: B
options.text: The author’s language in the quotation from Kokoro shows the character’s absorption in a task, while the language in the quotation from “The List” shows the character’s inattention to a task that must be completed.

options.label: C
options.text: The author’s language in the quotation from Kokoro suggests the character’s confidence about a successful outcome, while the language in the quotation from “The List” suggests the character’s insecurity about an outcome.

options.label: D
options.text: The author’s language in the quotation from Kokoro emphasizes the character’s commitment to completing a task, while the language in the quotation from “The List” emphasizes the character’s reluctance to begin a task.

visual_elements: From then on, my thesis hung over me like a curse, and with bloodshot eyes, I worked like a madman. (paragraph 9, from Kokoro)
Now, with school only a week away, Mia was left with just one skill: Learn to ride a unicycle. Shudder. (paragraph 6, “The List”)
